In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Norlane West Primary School.

At the end of 2010, Norlane West Primary School was closed as part of an agreed Regeneration Concept involving nine schools and the government. 

In the early 2000s, these nine schools, including Norlane West Primary School, sought government support to address their ageing infrastructure amid Victoria's population growth. Limited funding allocations meant significant regeneration was required, rather than smaller building updates. The Regeneration Concept was developed and led to the merging of the nine schools into the new Northern Bay P-12 College (School No. 8901) (VA 5358), forming what is claimed to be Victoria’s largest multi-campus school.

The first schools to merge were Rosewall Primary School (No. 5122) and Corio Primary (No. 124) in 2007 and in January 2011, the Northern Bay P-12 College was formed from the merger of:
  • Norlane West Primary School (No. 4880) became the West Campus
  • Corio Bay Senior Secondary College (No. 7105) became the Senior Campus and administration centre
  • Corio Primary School (No. 124) became the East Campus
  • Corio West Primary School (No. 5031) became the North Campus
  • North Shore Primary School (No. 4301) became the South Campus
  • Flinders Peak Secondary College (No. 7744; VA 5322) site was closed
  • Norlane High School (No. 8175) became Cox Road Campus
  • Corio South Primary School (No. 4927) became Corio South Primary Campus
Norlane West Primary School (School No. 4880) should not be confused with Norlane Primary School (School No. 4734) (VA 4629) which operated from 1955 to 1996.
name.official_title.title: Norlane West State School
title: Norlane West Primary School (School No. 4880; previously known as Norlane West State School 1962 - 1970)

description:
Located in Alberton in Wellington Shire, Gippsland, Alberton Primary School has been in continuous operation for over 150 years. It first opened as a National School in 1858 in a schoolhouse made of wattle and daub, with heavy galvanised iron on the outer walls. Enrolment at the time was 43.
In 1862, the Victorian Parliament abolished the two existing centralised boards and created a single Board of Education (VA 713) through the Common Schools Act.  With the passing of this act, the school was re-named Alberton Common School and was given the number 1.  

The size of the school grounds was increased by two acres in 1863, and by a further acre in both 1917 and 1949.
The Education Act of 1872 established the Victorian Education Department (VA 714) which marked further change to school naming conventions, with the school becoming Alberton State School. The school number was retained.
In 1891-1892 a brick schoolhouse was built to replace the old building. By the 1950s it had fallen into disrepair and a series of repairs were carried out. Despite this, the brick building was condemned in 1967 and replaced by a new timber construction.

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school’s name was changed to Alberton Primary School. 
In 2009 the school was completely rebuilt, adding a new Science/Art building and a new modular building used for Music.

As of 2023 there was an enrolment of 85.

Alberton Primary School is still in operation as of 2025.
title: Alberton Primary School (School No. 1; previously known as Alberton National School 1858-1862, Alberton Common School 1862-c.1872, Alberton State School c.1872-c.1970)

description:
Apollo Parkways Primary School (School No. 5184) (VA 5443) is a co-educational primary school located in Greensborough, in the northern suburbs of Melbourne. It first opened on 5th February 1979.

In 2008, a fire during school holidays destroyed three classrooms and the office area. The school grounds include an indoor stadium, three main buildings, several portable structures, three adventure playgrounds, two basketball and netball courts and an oval, as reported in 2022. 

As of 2025, Apollo Parkways Primary School is still operating, with approximately 680 students enrolled.
title: Apollo Parkways Primary School (School No. 5184)

description:
The Malmsbury Cemetery Trust was officially established in 1860 (Victoria Government Gazette 38, 19 March 1860).

The land for the cemetery had been set aside in 1859, however the site wasn't formally gazetted for the cemetery until 1861 (Victoria Government Gazette 22, 15 February 1861). The original site comprised 12 acres in the parish of Edgecombe and county of Talbot. The cemetery is on Cemetery Road in Malmsbury, approximately 100 km north of Melbourne.

Despite the first known burial at the cemetery occurring in 1860 burials were not officially recorded in the cemetery's burial register until 1862.
title: Malmsbury Cemetery Trust

description:
Altona Primary School first opened as Altona State School (School No. 3923) (VA 5445) in 1915, located in Melbourne’s south-western suburb of Altona.  The school originally operated out of a leased building or hall in the backyard of a local resident, with an enrolment of approximately 13 students.   

As enrolments increased, the school relocated around 1918 to the Progress Hall in Blyth Street. The hall was divided into two sections using a canvas blind across the centre of the building. By 1922, attendance had grown to around 160 students, and additional classes were held in nearby tea rooms and a café.

Following advocacy by the school committee and local state government members, a permanent school building was constructed on the corner of Blyth and Upton Streets. The new school opened in November 1922 with 225 students. The building reflected the typical Interwar Government school style, being red brick and stucco construction, with a Marseilles pattern tiled hipped roof.

Further additions in 1926–27 included an extended corridor running east and north, linking three classrooms. A new, enlarged cloak and hat room, along with a large teachers’ room, were also added. A shelter shed was constructed around the same time.

In 1954, a Bristol unit (so named because it was imported from England) was installed on the site, followed by the addition of four light timber construction classrooms in 1955 and another five by 1966. A library was built in 1972, and by 1973, enrolments had reached 595 students.

At some point, the name changed from state to primary. This likely occurred in 1970, as there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Altona Primary School. 

In 2018, a new modular building was introduced to replace the existing library.

As of 2025, the Altona Primary School is still in operation.
title: Altona Primary School (School No. 3923; previously known as Altona State School 1915 – 1970?)

description:
Doomburrim State School (School No. 3428) (VA 5446) was a coeducational primary school located in the Parish of Doomburrim, in the West Gippsland region of Victoria.

It first opened in 1902 out of small leased wooden building, and was worked part-time with Dumbalk South State School (School No. 3276). When Dumbalk South State School closed in 1904, Doomburrim was worked half-time instead with Meeniyan East State School (School No. 3240; later known as Buffalo State School) (VA 5447).

In 1909, Doomburrim State School became a full-time school and in 1911, it was proposed to build a new school. Two acres were acquired accordingly, and the new wooden school was completed in 1913.

Doomburrim State School was closed in 1945, and it is likely that the school building was removed in the following years and re-erected for West Tarwin Road State School (School No. 3405).

Note that Doomburrim may occasionally appear in records from the time as Doomburrin.
title: Doomburrim State School (School No. 3428)

description:
Ascot Vale Primary School (School No. 2608) (VA 5448) is a co-educational primary school situated in the inner north-west of Melbourne, part of the Moonee Valley network of schools.

The school was first established as Ascot Vale State School in order to replace the Flemington National School (School No. 250), which had become too small for the growing community. In 1882, it was recommended that a larger site be obtained to replace the Flemington School and in 1884, six brick classrooms were built on a site obtained by the Education Department (VA 714) on Bank St, to accommodate 452 students. The Flemington School was closed on 31st March 1885, with all teachers transferring immediately to the new Ascot Vale school on 1st April 1885. The new school was named Ascot Vale to distinguish it from the Flemington School, which was expected to (and later did) reopen. 

Enrolments at Ascot Vale State School grew to 600 by 1887, and classes were taught in the nearby Masonic Hall until more classrooms were built in 1888. By 1907 there were 921 students enrolled, and classes were run in additional private premises outside school grounds, including at the Congregational Church Hall and the old Melbourne College building. 1n 1910, the Education Department purchased additional land along the school’s western boundary to increase space.

In 1923, Ascot Vale West State School (School No. 4025) was opened, to help meet some of the enrolment demand, though Ascot Vale State School remained crowded for some time.

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term “State school” to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use “primary school” in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Ascot Vale Primary School. 

In 1984, a fire at the school caused damage to six classrooms and additional rooms, replaced by portable rooms at the time. 

As of 2025, Ascot Vale Primary School continues to operate out of the original school buildings between Bank St and Moonee St, with an enrolment of around 270 students.
title: Ascot Vale Primary School (School No. 2608; also known as Bank Street School; previously known as Ascot Vale State School 1885 – c. 1970)

description:
Aberfeldie Primary School (School No. 4220) (VA 5449) is a co-educational primary school located in the inner north-west of Melbourne. 

The school first opened in September 1925 as Aberfeldie State School, with 100 pupils taught from four classrooms. It expanded so quickly that two more classrooms were added the following year. 

Early on, Aberfeldie State School benefited greatly from engaged parent organisations. The Men’s Club built and contributed £300 worth of equipment for a craft-room, the first in a Victorian primary school, and the Mothers’ Club established a well-equipped sick bay.

In 1949, however, much of the school property was damaged by a significant fire. Fundraising activities were held in the nearby Essendon High School Hall. In 1950 two Bristol prefabricated schoolroom units were erected, and in 1951 further reconstruction of the school was funded by the State Government. By 1954 many of the amenities had been replaced. In 1959, the Education Department (VA 714) authorised a special grant of £1, 323 to the Aberfeldie State School Committee towards the erection of a new craft room at the school. A new sports field was also opened in 1965. 

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term “State school” to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use “primary school” in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Ascot Vale Primary School. 

In April 1997, Doutta Galla Primary School (School No. 4708) merged with Aberfeldie Primary School on the Aberfeldie site, continuing on as School No. 4220.

The school received funding in the 2016-17 and 2018-19 State Budgets for upgrades and modernisations to the existing school facilities. 

In 2025, Aberfeldie Primary School celebrates its centenary. At this time, it continues to operate on the same site, with almost 400 students enrolled.
title: Aberfeldie Primary School (School No. 4220; previously known as Aberfeldie State School 1925 – c.1970)

description:
Newham Primary School (School No. 1913) (VA 5451) is a co-educational primary school located in the Macedon Ranges.

It first opened in June 1877, as Newham State School. It replaced the Presbyterian National School No. 465, later called Newham Common School, which had operated in the area since 1860, and which was officially closed as of 31st May 1877. 

A wooden schoolroom with quarters attached was built for the new state school. Additions were made to the residence in 1908 and the schoolroom in 1910.  

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Newham Primary School. 

In 2010, Newham Primary School received a new school building as part of the Rural Replacement Program, which was an initiative of the Victorian government to secure the future of small rural schools in their communities with purpose-designed permanent buildings.  

As of 2025, Newham Primary School continues to operate, with an enrolment of approximately 54 students.
title: Newham Primary School (School No. 1913; previously known as Newham State School 1877 – c.1970)

description:
Banyule Primary School (School No. 4746) (VA 5452) is a co-educational primary school located in Rosanna, in Melbourne’s northern suburbs, in the city of Banyule.

It first opened in 1960 as Banyule State School, on a piece of land purchased by the Education Department in 1954. It was originally comprised of six classrooms, but as enrolments grew additional classrooms were added in 1962 and 1964.

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Banyule Primary School. 

As of 2025, Banyule Primary School continues to operate, with approximately 640 students reportedly enrolled in 2024.
title: Banyule Primary School (School No. 4746; previously known as Banyule State School 1960 – c. 1970)

description:
Rosebud Secondary College (School No. 8290) (VA 5453) is a co-educational high school located in the Southern Mornington Peninsula.

A site for a new high school on Boneo Rd, Rosebud, was first approved in 1943, however the school did not open for another ten years. It finally opened in February 1954 as Rosebud High School, with close to 300 students. The buildings consisted of a Bristol prefabricated building with seven rooms, a five-room timber building, and a library.

The site was significantly developed over the next decade, with a number of new additions including gardens and playgrounds, administration and domestic arts units, a music/arts and crafts wing, four more classrooms, a science wing, and an assembly hall. 

In 1990, the school underwent a name change to Rosebud Secondary College following the Change of School Name and Reclassification of Schools Executive Memorandum No 314 from the Ministry of Education (VA 1112). 

In the late 2010s and 2020s, Rosebud Secondary College went through another significant period of development. In 2020, the school built an inclusive outdoor space with a collaborate learning area and sensory garden, funded as part of the State government’s 2018 Inclusive Schools Fund. In 2021, the school was supported by the School Pride and Sports Fund to build a wellness centre. In the 2021-21 State Budget, the school received $10 million for significant upgrades and modernisations. Two new learning buildings were completed accordingly in 2023.

Rosebud Secondary College has strong links with the Rosebud Rotary Club and has done since the Club began presenting citizenship prizes to students in 1955. The school also partners with the Mornington Peninsula Foundation, a philanthropic organisation established in 2017 supporting a range of initiatives in the Western Port and Southern Peninsula regions. 

As of 2025, Rosebud Secondary College continues to operate, with approximately 900 students enrolled.
title: Rosebud Secondary College (School No. 8290; previously known as Rosebud High School 1954 - 1990)

description:
Appin South Primary School (School No. 3495) (VA 5454) was a co-educational government primary school located in the rural locality of Appin, approximately 230 km north of Melbourne.

The school opened in February 1905 as Appin South State School and may also have been known as Appin South Leased School. It initially operated from a leased room measuring 28 ft by 12 ft in a local resident’s home. Enrolment for the opening year was 30 students.

In April 1906, a school building with an attached teacher’s residence was relocated from the former Reedy Lake State School (School No. 2461) to a two-acre site on another resident’s property, and the school reopened as Appin South State School. This building remained in use until 1924, when it was relocated to Appin Primary School (School No. 2351) (VA 3345). In the same year, a new school building, without a teacher’s residence, was constructed on a new site adjacent to the public hall.

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to broaden the use of the term ‘State School’ to include all government schools, rather than referring exclusively to primary-level schools. Subsequently, all primary schools began to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Appin South Primary School around this time.

Appin South Primary School became unstaffed in 1984. Under departmental policy, schools with low or no enrolments could be destaffed, allowing for the possibility of reopening if enrolments increased. Following a period of destaffing, the school was permanently closed by the Education Minister in January 1985. The property and buildings were sold by public auction in 1986.

Appin South Primary School should not be confused with Appin Park State School (School No. 5207) (VA 5344), which opened in 1982 and continues to operate as of 2026, or Appin State School (School No. 2351) (VA 3345), also known as Lake Merring State School, which opened in 1881 and closed in 1973.
title: Appin South Primary School (School No. 3495; previously known as Appin South State School 1905 – 1970)

description:
Beulah Primary School (School No. 3109) (VA 5455) is a small rural co-educational primary school located in the Southern Mallee region of Victoria. 

It first opened in 1891 as Galaquil State School, operating out of a single building on the corner of Hopetoun Road and Bell Street. One year later, the school name was changed to Beulah State School. That same year, a second building was moved to Beulah from the closed Heatherlie State School (School No. 2910), with a new section added to it in 1899. 

In 1930, a new brick school was opened, with three classrooms, an office and a storeroom, and an adjacent wooden classroom was added in 1963.

In 1950, the nearby school Galaquil State School (School No. 3083) (VA 5342), was closed due to a damaged school building, and the primary school students who had attended it were sent to both Beulah and Brim State School (School No. 2995) (VA 4620).

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Beulah Primary School.

As of 2025, Beulah Primary School is still in operation, with 23 students enrolled. It works closely with other schools in the Southern Mallee Cluster, to provide a wider range of social, sporting and educational opportunities for its students. 

Beulah Primary School (formerly named Galaquil State School from 1891 – 1892) should not be confused with Galaquil State School (School No. 3083) (VA 5342), which operated in the same area from 1891 to 1950.
title: Beulah Primary School (School No. 3109; previously known as Galaquil State School 1891 – 1892; Beulah State School 1895 – c.1970)

description:
Port Fairy Consolidated School is a coeducational primary school located in the coastal community of Port Fairy, in the Moyne Shire of South West Victoria.

The town was originally called Belfast, and the first schools in the region were largely private and supported by specific denominational groups. They included a Church of England School (Common School No. 62), established in 1856, and a Wesleyan School (Common School No. 83), established in 1857; both schools were closed and absorbed into the new Belfast State School No. 1188 in 1873.

The school first ran in the former premises of the Church of England school, leased at a half-yearly rental of £15; when the Wesleyan School closed, its premises was also rented. Attendance rapidly increased from 154 pupils to more than 250.

Plans for a stone building to accommodate 500 children on a site of two acres of Crown Land were prepared the same year, and after two calls for tenders the contract let for £3,470. Stone for the building was quarried on the site. Labour disputes delayed completion, however permission was granted to move the school into the new building on 11th of November 1874, although it was not yet finished.
In 1887, a special Act of parliament renamed the town—and subsequently the school—Port Fairy.

Port Fairy State School became a Higher Elementary School in 1925 before closing in 1948. The same year, a move was made to consolidate a number of small country schools in the area into one large school. Port Fairy was chosen as the ‘Mother’ school and consolidated the closed schools of Orford (No. 1374), Rosebrook (No. 526), Moyne (No. 3677), Yambuk (No. 2458), and Toolong (No. 3595). On February 1st 1949 the school officially became the Port Fairy Consolidated School.

Until consolidation, the bluestone building remained substantially the same as when it was built in 1874. Major alterations and additions were made in the subsequent 14 years. Two school buildings from schools in Moyne and Dean were brought in and sited to the west of the main building. These were equipped for teaching sheetmetal and woodwork. A wing of five classrooms, a sick bay and two small storerooms were added. In 1961 a new woodwork room was built.

Further additions and modernisations have been made in the decades since. The school is now a mix of original bluestone buildings and modern teaching and learning spaces.  These include nine classrooms, a dedicated art studio, a STEM building, an instrumental music room, a fully equipped kitchen, a multi-purpose hall, and a café/kitchen area. Additionally, the grounds incorporate two large sporting ovals, two basketball courts, and multiple play areas. 

Sometime between 1973–1975 the school number was changed from 1188 to 6247.
This school is still in operation as of 2025.
title: Port Fairy Consolidated School (School No. 6247; previously known as Belfast State School 1873-1887; Port Fairy State School 1887-1925; Port Fairy Higher Elementary School, 1925-1948; School No. 1188, 1873-c.1974)

description:
Wonyip State School (School No. 3509) (VA 5457) was established in 1905 as Wonyip North State School.  Located in Victoria’s South Gippsland region, the school operated from the leased Excelsior Hall. The hall was destroyed by bushfire in March 1906 and it is likely classes recommenced once the hall was rebuilt. 

In 1908, the school name was changed to Wonyip State School, retaining the school number 3509.  The school experienced periods of temporary closure.  It appears to have closed from February to April 1911, and likely operated part-time with Binginwarri State School (School No. 2863) from July 1912 to July 1914, before returning to full time status following an increase in enrolments. 

A permanent site was purchased around 1919, and a new building was erected there in 1922. The new premises were occupied in March 1923, and the lease on Excelsior Hall was ended.

The school again closed in December 1927 due to low enrolment.  The buildings were removed and re-erected to Port Franklin State School (School No. 4280) (VA 5391) in 1929, and the Wonyip site was formally revoked in 1930. 

In July 1940, Wonyip State School reopened, again operating from the leased Excelsior Hall.  The school was closed from December 1951 to June 1953, and appears to have been unstaffed from 1954 to 1955.

By 1973, enrolments had fallen to just seven students, and the school was permanently closed in 1974.

Wonyip State School (No. 3509) should not be confused with the former Woorarra Primary School (School No. 3410) (VA 5395), which was known as Wonyip State School from 1902 to 1908.
title: Wonyip State School (School No. 3509; previously known as Wonyip North State School 1905 – 1908)

description:
Albert Park Primary School (School No. 1181) (VA 5458) is a co-educational primary school located in the City of Port Phillip.

The school first opened in January 1873, with 654 students enrolled. Until a building could be provided, it initially operated out of two temporary accommodations: the local Mechanics Institute and the Orderly Room of the Emerald Hill Artillery. In 1874, a new building was completed for the school on Nelson Road, with classes commencing on that site from April 1874. While the school has remained on that site, the facilities have evolved considerably over time to meet enrolment demands and as the surrounding area changed.

By 1886, enrolments had exceeded 1500 students, and the original building was no longer sufficient. In 1887, the nearby Middle Park State School (School No. 2815) was opened, which was hoped would alleviate some of the pressure. By 1900 however, three rooms had to be leased by the Education Department (VA 714) from the Wesleyan Church in Cardigan Place to house the overflow of students from Albert Park. While initially a lease for 6-12 months, the lease remained for the next 13 years. In 1901, proposals were put forward to build a separate Infant School in Henderson St. This was eventually completed in 1914. In 1907, alterations were made to the main school, and during the works children were taught in leased spaces in the Dorcas Street Presbyterian Church buildings, and the Presbyterian Church on the corner of Merton and O’Grady Streets.

From 1968, the primary school shared its facilities with staff and students of the new South Melbourne High School (later known as Albert Park High School). In 1970, temporary arrangements were made to close off Bridport Street during school hours to provide additional playground space. In 1971 the closure was made official through an Act of Parliament, with the space being incorporated into the school grounds. Also in 1970, the Education Department purchased the Methodist Church Hall on Cardigan Place for the school, which had been used as overflow teaching space for some time. The High School moved to its own premises at the end of 1971.

A new library and arts centre was completed in 1998, and several portable classrooms have been erected in the years since then. In 2013, the City of Port Phillip Council (VA 3716) closed off a section Moubray Street to traffic, creating a park that the school shares with the public.

Albert Park Primary School has had several different names during its history. At the time of commencement, it was known variously as both the Emerald Hill and Mechanics’ Institute State School, reflecting the location of classes. When schooling moved into the new building in 1874, the school was renamed Nelson Road State School. The exact year when the school became officially known as Albert Park State School remains subject to further research, however it appears as such in Government Gazettes from as early as 1897. In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Albert Park Primary School. 

As of 2025, Albert Park Primary School continues to operate, with an enrolment of approximately 500 students.
title: Albert Park Primary School (School No. 1181; previously known as Emerald Hill State School and Mechanics’ Institute State School 1873 - 1874; Nelson Road State School 1874 – c. 1897; Albert Park State School c.1897 – c.1970)

description:
Cocongella Common School opened in 1872 with an initial enrolment of 32 students. It is situated in a rural setting on a 2.5-acre block approximately two miles east of Stawell, in the Wimmera region of western Victoria. The school operated from a newly constructed single-room red brick building. Night classes were also held on the premises.

Between 1873 and 1878 the school became Concongella State School, following the implementation of the Education Act (Vic) 1872, which established the Victorian Education Department (VA 714) and introduced new school naming conventions. 

By 1887, attendance had grown to 57 students.  In 1907, parents paid to have the gallery removed.

By the 1940s, attendance had dropped to eight students. Enrolments rose again to 43 students by 1961, and some classes were held in the supper room of the local hall.

Around 1970, the name changed again to Concongella Primary School, in line with a statewide decision to broaden the use of the term ‘State School’ to include all government schools, rather than referring exclusively to primary-level schools. Subsequently, all primary schools began to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. 

As of 2003, the school site included the original red brick school building, which remained centrally located, alongside more recent portable classrooms, toilet facilities, and outbuildings.

As of 2025, Cocongella Primary School is still in operation with the original brick building still in use.
title: Concongella Primary School (School No. 1136; previously known as Cocongella Common School 1872 – C.1875; Cocongella State School C. 1875 – C. 1970)

description:
Bittern Primary School (School No. 3933) (VA 5430) is a co-educational primary school located in a semi-rural setting on the Mornington Peninsula, approximately 82 kilometres from Melbourne. The school first opened as Bittern State School in July 1916, operating from a leased hall with an initial enrolment of 12 students.

In 1919, the Education Department (VA 714) purchased a one-acre site to establish a permanent location for the school. The following year, in 1920, the school relocated from the leased hall to a newly constructed wooden building on the new site. At the time of the move, enrolment had increased to 40 students. A second room was added in April 1959 to accommodate growing enrolments, and a five-room teacher’s residence was constructed in 1965.

At some stage, the name changed from state to primary. This likely occurred in 1970, as there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Bittern Primary School. 

Under the 2022–23 State Budget, Bittern Primary School received funding for upgrade and modernisation works, including refurbishment of the library and replacement of old relocatable buildings with new relocatable classrooms. The school is also progressing through a Capital Works Project to construct a new learning centre with four classrooms and an outdoor learning space.  As of 2023, the school had an enrolment of 73 students.  

In 2025, Bittern Primary School is still in operation.
title: Bittern Primary School (School No. 3933; previously known as Bittern State School 1916 – c.1970)

description:
Ballarat Specialist School (School No. 4762) (VA 5461) opened as Ballarat Special School in February 1955 as an annex at Pleasant Street Primary School (School No. 695), with an initial enrolment of 38 students. 

In 1963, enrolment had increased to 42, and the school moved to a new site on Inkerman Street. A five-acre pine plantation was established at the rear of the site though whether it was later milled under the School Endowment Pine Plantation scheme is subject to further research.

By 1967, enrolments had reached 90, and a portable classroom providing two additional rooms was added. In 1969, enrolments had grown to 108, with the school comprising the original building and four portable classrooms.

In 1982, the school relocated to the Gillies Street Campus. Enrolments at the time were around 90 students.  The 1990s marked a significant era of transformation in education throughout Victoria, as the Jeff Kennett government initiated numerous school closures and mergers across the state.

Ballarat Special School was renamed Begonia Park School in 1991. In 1993, it began sharing the Gillies Street site with Ballarat Special Developmental School (School No. 5274), which had previously been known as McCallum House or Austin McCallum Special Developmental School. Although both schools continued to operate independently initially, a protracted merger process began between 1996 and 1998. The school councils formally combined in 1997, and the schools officially merged in 1998 to form Ballarat Specialist School, retaining the school number 4762.

In June 2008, Ballarat Specialist School acquired the FARM campus.  By 2020, enrolments had exceeded 450. As of 2025, Ballarat Specialist School remains operational, with two campuses: Gillies Street (main campus) and the FARM / Senior Campus.

Note: Ballarat Special School should not be confused with the former Ballarat Special Developmental School (School No. 5274) which operated nearby from 1988 to 1998 when it merged with Ballarat Special School (then known as Begonia Park School) to form Ballarat Specialist School.
title: Ballarat Specialist School (School No. 4762; previously known as Ballarat Special School 1955 – 1991; Begonia Park School 1991 – 1998)

description:
Birregurra Primary School (School No. 723) (VA 5451) is a co-educational primary school located in the township of Birregurra, in Colac Otway Shire.

It first opened as a common school in 1863. Birregurra Common School operated out of the Methodist Church Hall until 1865, when a new school building made out of locally fired bricks was erected. 

Around 1873, the school changed its name to Birregurra State School. This was due to the Education Act (Vic) 1872, which established the Victorian Education Department (VA 714) and a subsequent change to school naming conventions.

In 1926, additions were made to the original school building, and in 1948, when the schoolhouse was deemed unsafe, attempts were made to support the structure of the building with iron rods and timber. This was unsuccessful, however, and a new school building was erected in 1950.

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Birregurra Primary School. 

In the 2020-21 State Budget, the school received $2.212 million for upgrades and modernisation. Capital works upgrades in 2023 saw the construction of a new main building, and the demolition of most of the old building to create open space. As of 2025, Birregurra Primary School continues to operate, with an enrolment of approximately 110 students.
title: Birregurra Primary School (School No. 723; previously known as Birregurra Common School 1863 – c.1873; Birregurra State School c.1873 – 1970)

description:
Bass Valley Primary School (School No. 5159) (VA 5195) is a rural coeducational primary school located in the Bass Coast region of southern Victoria, just out of Corinella. 

The school was first opened in February 1979. It was the result of the government’s consolidation policy for rural schools, which saw the closure of the following schools in the region, with all students moving to the new Bass Valley Primary School:  
  • Bass Primary School (School No. 847)
  • Corinella Primary School (School No. 1392)
  • Grantville Primary School (School No. 1414)
  • Kernot Primary School (School No. 4024)
  • Kilcunda Primary School (School No. 2307)
  • Woodleigh Primary School (School No. 2463)
  • Woolamai Primary School (School No. 3856)

In 2000, the school facilities received a significant redevelopment, the result of an almost $2 million capital works project. 

As of 2025, Bass Valley Primary School continues to operate, with approximately 240 students.
title: Bass Valley Primary School (School No. 5195)

description:
Colac High School (School No. 7740) (VA 5464) was a government secondary school located in Colac, a town in the Western District of Victoria, approximately 150 kilometres south-west of Melbourne on the southern shore of Lake Colac.

The school opened in January 1911 as Colac Agricultural High School. It was established during a period when the Victorian Education Department promoted rural secondary education with a curriculum combining general academic subjects and agricultural science, practical farming, and experimental work.

The school initially operated from temporary leased premises with an opening enrolment of 61 students. In 1912, it relocated to a newly constructed building on land donated to the Education Department (VA 714).

In 1924, two additional rooms were constructed. In June 1927, the school farm was closed and the school name changed to Colac High School. A further three rooms were added in 1928.

In 1951, two Bristol prefabricated classrooms were added to the site. Two additional light timber construction classrooms were constructed in 1952. In 1959, a manual arts wing and a science wing were added.

The assembly hall officially opened in 1967. Subsequent additions included a Commonwealth Science Block, Humanities Wing, and Domestic Science Wing. A Year 12 Common Room was added in 1974, followed by a Commonwealth Library in 1975. In 1980, a portable band room was installed.

In December 2007, Colac High School merged with Colac College (School No. 7095) to form Colac Secondary College (School No. 8864), effective from January 2008. The new multi-campus school relocated to Queen Street.

In 2024, Lake Colac School (School No. 5247) relocated to the former Colac High School site.
title: Colac High School (School No. 7740; previously known as Colac Agricultural High School 1911 – 1927)

description:
Beaconsfield Upper Primary School (School No. 2560) (VA 5465) is a co-educational primary school located in a semi-rural community east of Melbourne, around 10kms north of Berwick.

A school was first established in Upper Beaconsfield in late 1883. The school was built to the north of the Upper Beaconsfield township, as that was where the greater number of children lived. The original building was a single-room weatherboard structure, and the original name was Beaconsfield North State School. 

Within a few years, the schoolhouse was deemed not suitable for teaching, with its location close to Stoney Creek exposing students to snakes in summer and the cold in winter. It seems that to account for this, a second school ran for a time out of the Upper Beaconsfield Hall. This appears to have been independent from the Beaconsfield Upper school, though it remains subject to further research. 

In 1915, a new school was eventually built further south, on the site still used in 2025. By this time the school had become known as Beaconsfield Upper, or Upper Beaconsfield, State School. The exact year the name officially changed is unclear. A teacher residence was built in 1952, and additional rooms were built to meet growing enrolments throughout the 1950s and 1960s. 

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Beaconsfield Upper Primary School. 

As of 2025, Beaconsfield Upper Primary School continues to operate, with approximately 340 students. A new inclusive playground is due to be completed in 2025, supported by the Victorian Government’s Inclusive Schools Fund.
title: Beaconsfield Upper Primary School (School No. 2560; also known as Upper Beaconsfield Primary School; previously known as Beaconsfield North State School 1883 – c.1915; Beaconsfield Upper State School 1915 – c.1970)

description:
Mount Best Primary School (School No. 3429) (VA 5466) was a co-educational primary school which opened as Mount Best State School in June 1902. The school was located at the top of Mount Best in the South Gippsland region of Victoria. 

In January of 1906, the school was destroyed in the Black Thursday fires. Following this disaster, it was conducted part-time from a private house for some months, before relocating to the local Church, where it remained from 1907 to late 1909. The school then operated out of a leased Mechanic’s Institute Hall from 1910 until 1923, when a new site was donated to the school and a new building was erected.

In 1924, the Education Department (VA 714) sold the original school site which had been burned in the Black Thursday fires. In 1940, the school again lost property in bushfires, this time out-offices, fencing and forest areas were destroyed but the main school building was saved. 

A teachers’ residence was added to the site in 1952.

At some stage the name changed from State to Primary. This likely occurred in 1970, as there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term “State School”. "State School" now referred to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools. And all primary schools now included "Primary School" in its name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Mount Best Primary School. 

Mount Best Primary School was permanently closed in late December 1989 and likely merged into Toora Primary School (School No. 2253).
title: Mount Best Primary School (School No. 3429; previously known as Mount Best State School 1902 – c. 1970)

description:
Yuille Park Community College (School No. 5520) (VA 5467) is a coeducational school located in Wendouree, in the northern suburbs of Ballarat.  

The school was established in 2007, when Yuille Primary School (School No. 5198) and Grevillea Park Primary School (School No. 4701) were closed and merged. The new school was initially called Yuille/Grevillea Park Primary School, before changing its name to Yuille Park P-8 Community College in 2008 when secondary classes were added. In 2024, the name was officially changed again to Yuille Park Community College.

Across its two campuses, the school presently runs a flexible learning curriculum from pre-school to secondary school. The Grevillea Campus includes a Children’s Centre for three- and four-year-olds alongside classes from Prep to Year 8. The Yuille Campus offers a flexible learning option for ages 12 – 20 (year 7 to year 12), and the Yuille Park Young Parents Campus offers young pregnant or parenting students the opportunity to study at a Senior Secondary Level, including VCAL.

As of 2025, Yuille Park Community College continues to operate.
title: Yuille Park Community College (School No. 5520; previously known as Yuille/Grevillea Park Primary School 2007 – 2008; Yuille Park P-8 Community College 2008 - 2024)

description:
Mitta Mitta Primary School (School No. 887) (VA 5468) is a small co-educational primary school located in the northeast of Victoria. It is 60km from Tallangatta and 81km from Wodonga, and services the rural communities of Dartmouth and Mitta Mitta. 

It was first established in 1869 as Junction, Snowy Creek Common School, under the Board of Education (VA 713). The name reflected how the area was known at the time and was meant to distinguish the school from Snowy Creek, which was a nearby village. It seems, however, that both “Junction, Snowy Creek” and “Snowy Creek” were used interchangeably to refer to School No. 887. 

In May 1870, the local committee applied to the Board of Education for funding towards a new wooden school building, but this was mistakenly thought to be an application for a new school. School No. 1044, also called “Junction, Snowy Creek”, was registered accordingly, only to be cancelled once the mistake was realised. 

The Education Act of 1872 established the Victorian Education Department (VA 714) which marked a change to school naming conventions, with the school becoming Junction, Snowy Creek State School. In 1880, the town was officially gazetted as Mitta Mitta Village, and the school name was changed to Mitta Mitta State School that same year,

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Mitta Mitta Primary School.

As of 2025, Mitta Mitta Primary School continues to operate, with one class of P-6 students. 

Mitta Mitta Primary School should not be confused with the nearby schools Mitta North Primary School (School No. 3974), which operated from 1918 until 1988, and Little Snowy Creek Primary School (School No. 3027) (VA 3356), which operated from 1890 to 1983, or with Junction, Snowy Creek State School (School No. 1044) which was registered in 1870 but never officially established.
title: Mitta Mitta Primary School (School No. 887; previously known as Junction, Snowy Creek Common School 1869 – c.1873; Junction, Snowy Creek State School c.1873 – 1880; Mitta Mitta State School 1880 – c.1970)

description:
Murchison Primary School (School No. 1126) (VA 5469) is a coeducational primary school located in the Goulburn Valley region of northern Victoria. 

Murchison Primary School was preceded by a Presbyterian School which opened in 1859 in Murchison. This school became a Common School in 1862, through the Common Schools Act, and was assigned the number 420. The school building for Common School No. 420 was, however, blown down by a storm on 17 December 1870 and was subsequently closed. It was replaced by the new Murchison Common School, with the new Victorian school number of 1126, on a new site on Willoughby Street, in November 1871.

The Education Act of 1872 established the Victorian Education Department (VA 714) which marked a change to school naming conventions, with the school becoming Murchison State School.

In 1896, requests were made for a new school building and in 1901 land was purchased for this purpose, with a brick building erected on Impey Street. The new building was officially opened in 1906, and the former school buildings were repurposed as a sloyd woodworking room and cookery centre. 

In 1949, memorial gates were erected at the front of the school, and sometime during that similar period, an additional timber school building was brought to Murchison from Mitchellstown State School (School No. 1750), which had closed in 1943.

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Murchison Primary School.

In 2024, an inclusive playground was built on the grounds and as of 2025, Murchison Primary School continues to operate.

Murchison Primary School should not be confused with school that preceded it, Murchison Common School (School No. 420), which operated in the area from 1859 – 1870.
title: Murchison Primary School (School No. 1126; previously known as Murchison Common School 1871 – 1872; Murchison State School 1872 – c.1970)

description:
Sherbrooke Community School (School No. 6252) (VA 5470) is a small coeducational Prep to Year 12 school located in the township of Sassafras, in the Dandenong Ranges, south-east of Melbourne. It was founded in 1985.

As of 2025, Sherbrooke Community School continues to operate, and in the 2025-26 State Budget received funding to plan and design a new modernised learning facility, including STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts, mathematics) spaces.
title: Sherbrooke Community School (School No. 6252)

description:
Rochester Primary School (School No. 795) (VA 5471) is a coeducational primary school located in the Goulburn Murray region of northern Victoria. 

The school first opened in 1865 as Rochester Common School. In 1872, the new Education Act established the Victorian Education Department (VA 714) which marked a change to school naming conventions, with the school becoming Rochester State School. 

In 1879, a Night School was established at the school, and in 1923 Rochester extended to become a Higher Elementary School (HES), with senior classes operating under the same head teacher as the State school and an additional senior master. From 1 January 1957, the HES was officially declared Rochester High School, continuing to co-exist on the Rochester State School premises.

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Rochester Primary School.

The physical premises of Rochester Primary School changed many times throughout its history. From 1865, it originally operated out of a single-room wooden building with a bark roof on High Street and could accommodate approximately 20 students. In 1874, the Education Department built a new brick schoolhouse to replace the original wooden one, to accommodate 120 students, however the site was poorly situated and was subject to floods and diseases, requiring the school to be closed on several occasions. Increasing enrolments also meant that the size became insufficient, and in 1884 a new brick building was erected on the Recreation Reserve to accommodate 187 students, known informally as the ‘Rec’ School. Unfortunately, this building continued to have the same problems as its predecessor and in 1914, a contract to build a new school in Edward Street was awarded. 

The new school building on Edward Street was officially opened in February 1915. As enrolments continued to grow, several buildings from surrounding rural schools were relocated to the Rochester site, including from schools at Tennyson and Nanneella. In 1917, a teacher’s residence was built. The previous ‘Rec’ School building continued to be used as additional classroom spaces for the Higher Elementary School for a number of years, particularly for Sloyd (woodworking) classes. It was later also used by the local Football Club before being demolished in 1962.

Additional classrooms were added in 1965 and 1969, and in 1973 a combined Library/Art building was erected. In 2009, Rochester Primary School received funding through the federal Building the Education Revolution (BER) program, which went towards construction of a new building containing four classrooms, a resource area and two conference rooms.

Rochester Primary School was significantly affected by flooding in the region in 2022, with students beginning to return to the site in February 2023.

As of 2025, Rochester Primary School continues to operate, and continues to be co-located on the Edward Street site with Rochester Secondary College (School No. 8280).
title: Rochester Primary School (School No. 795; previously known as Rochester Common School 1865 – c.1872; Rochester State School c.1872 – c.1970)

description:
Carchap Primary School (School No. 2816) (VA 5472) was a government primary school located in the rural locality of Carchap in the Wimmera region, approximately 30 km south of Horsham in western Victoria.

The school opened in August 1887 as Carchap State School. It operated from a portable wooden school building with an attached teacher’s residence situated on two acres of land donated by a local resident.

From February 1896 to February 1900, Carchap State School operated part-time with Lowan South State School (School No. 2984), with a single teacher shared between the two schools and dividing their time between both sites. In 1902, a detached wooden kitchen was added to the site. It is likely that a railway line was constructed through part of the school grounds in 1911. Further building changes may also have occurred in 1927, although this is subject to further research.

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Carchap Primary School.

The school appears to have permanently closed between 1975 and 1984. The site was sold by public auction in 1988.
title: Carchap Primary School (School No. 2816; previously known as Carchap State School 1887 – circa 1970)

description:
Malvern Primary School (School No. 2586) (VA 5473) is a coeducational primary school located in the south-eastern Melbourne suburb of Malvern, part of the Stonnington & Glen Eira (SaGE) Network of Schools. 

The school first opened in April 1884 in a wooden building leased from the Church of England, opposite Caulfield railway station, and was at this time known as the Racecourse School. The lease was not renewed and the school subsequently closed from September 1885, reopening in July 1886 in a one-room brick building on Tooronga Road. From 1887 it became known as Malvern (Tooronga Road) State School. Additions made to the school buildings include a bell tower, Head Teachers office and several classrooms, and in 1908 an infant school building was opened. 

From 1927 to 1942, the school became Tooronga Road Central School, running the first two years of a high school course and acting as a feeder school for students to go on to a high school, such as Melbourne High School (School No. 8025). 

During World War II, the central grades were transferred to Lloyd Street Primary School (School No. 4139; previously known as Malvern East Central School) and third form Melbourne High School boys moved into the main Tooronga Road building for a year.

From 1946, the newly established Malvern Girls High School (School No. 8002) took over the southern section of the main building, and a free-standing domestic arts building was built on the site for the high school girls. In 1961, a double-storey building was constructed for a library, cookery centre and music room. Malvern Girls High School continued to use the primary school site until 1993, when it merged with Richmond Girls High School (School No. 8268) to form the Melbourne Girls' College (School No. 8819), and vacated the Tooronga Road site. 

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Malvern Primary School.

As of 2025, Malvern Primary School continues to operate, in the original buildings on the Tooronga Road site.

Malvern Primary School should not be confused with Malvern Central School (School No. 1604; previously known as Spring St, Malvern School) (VA 5207).
title: Malvern Primary School (School No. 2586; previously known as the Racecourse School 1884 – 1887; Malvern (Tooronga Road) State School 1887 – 1927 and 1942 – 1970; Tooronga Road Central School 1927 – 1942)

description:
St Matthew’s (Carlton) State School (School No. 559) (VA 5474) was opened by the Church of England in November 1855.  The co-educational primary school was located on Lygon Street, Carlton and had an average attendance of 19 boys and 15 girls in the opening year, accommodated in two separate buildings.  The schools were likely known separately as St Matthew’s Boys School and St Matthew’s Girls School. At the time of establishment, denominational or church-organised schools were supported by the Victorian colonial government under the Denominational School Board (VA 703). 

In 1862, with the dissolution of the Denominational School Board and the introduction of the single Board of Education (VA 713), the school was assigned the number 559. Ten years later, the Education Act 1872 established the Victorian Education Department (VA 714) and introduced free, compulsory and secular schooling for Victorian children. The school then became known as St Matthews State School.

In March 1874, St Matthew’s State School was closed and merged with Carlton (Drummond Street) State School (School No. 177) (VA 4447). The merged school retained the name Carlton State School and the number 177, continuing to operate across three sites — on Lygon Street, Drummond Street, and at Trades Hall. Prior to the merger, Carlton State School had operated as a girls’ school.
title: Carlton, St Matthew’s State School (School No. 559; previously known as St Matthew’s School, Lygon Street 1855 – 1873)

description:
Belmont High School (School No. 7585) (VA 5475) is a coeducational secondary school located in the Geelong suburb of Belmont.

The school was first opened in 1955, using temporary quarters at the Swanston Street Central School and in two prefabricated buildings at Geelong High School (School No. 7855). In September of that year, the school moved to a permanent building on Laura Ave, adjacent to Rosyln Primary School (School No. 4663). It was the second state high school to be established in Geelong. 

At its primary campus in Geelong, Belmont High School hosts the Victorian Bioscience Education Centre (BioLAB), a Statewide resource delivering specialist bioscience, health and sports science programs to schools across Victoria. The school also maintains a second campus in the Colac-Otway Shire (VA 3681), known as Tanybryn, which is used as a campsite.  

As of 2025, Belmont High School continues to operate, and is one of the largest schools in Geelong with approximately 1300 students.
title: Belmont High School (School No. 7585)

description:
Kurunjang Primary School (School No. 5256) (VA 5476) is a coeducational primary school located 35 kilometres northwest of Melbourne, in the northern area of Melton, adjacent to Kurunjang Secondary College in the Kurunjang Estate. It first opened in 1989.

In 2019, the City of Melton built a community hub next to the school, which the school is able to utilise for both curriculum activities and activities outside of school hours. 

As of 2025, Kurunjang Primary School continues to operate, with approximately 560 students.
title: Kurunjang Primary School (School No. 5256)

description:
The Disability Services Commissioner (DSC) was established in 2007 under the Disability Act 2006. It's primary role is to act as an independent complaints body, providing a free and confidential complaints resolution process. Under the Disability Amendment Act 2017, the role of the DSC was expanded to include greater investigation, inquiry and inspection powers.

The DSC is an independent oversight body for the Victorian disability sector and has responsibility for handling complaints, oversight of critical incidents, and conducting investigations into allegations of abuse, assault, and neglect.

DSC functions as outlined under Section 16 of the Disability Act 2006 include:

  • Assessing, conciliating or investigating complaints relating to disability services
  • Reviewing and identifying causes of complaints, and causes of abuse and neglect, and suggest ways of removing and minimising those causes
  • Maintaining a record of all complaints received and investigations conducted, and publishing information about these complaints and investigations
  • Providing advice, inquiring or investigating matters referred by the Minister or the Secretary
  • Providing education and information about the prevention and resolution of complaints, and the prevention of and responses to abuse and neglect
  • Conducting research into complaints, abuse and neglect in disability services.

DSC powers as outlined under Section 17 of the Disability Act 2006 include:

  • Consulting with any persons or bodies which the Commissioner considers appropriate
  • Developing and suggesting ways of implementing procedures for dealing with complaints relating to disability services, and preventing and responding to abuse and neglect of people with a disability
  • Providing advice on any matter relating to complaints, accountability investigations, and the prevention of and response to abuse and neglect in disability services
  • Seek information about complaints systems, and any systems in place to prevent and respond to abuse and neglect.

In addition to the above functions and powers, the Commissioner also has the power to conduct Commissioner initiated investigations (s. 128B), and appoint Authorised Officers who have the power to visit and inspect premises of disability service providers (s. 132B).
title: Disability Services Commissioner

description:
Heidelberg Primary School (School No. 294) (VA 5479), located in Melbourne’s north-eastern suburb of Heidelberg, is one of Victoria’s oldest schools. Established in August 1854 as a National School, it was also known as Heidelberg Girls’ School and Heidelberg Boys’ School, with 36 girls and 32 boys enrolled.  The school operated from a brick schoolroom, one for girls and another for boys with an attached teachers’ residence. 

In 1862, through the Common Schools Act, the Victorian Parliament abolished the two existing centralised boards (National (VA 919) and Denominational (VA 703)) and created a single Board of Education (VA 713).  With the passing of this act, the school was re-named Heidelberg Common School and was given the number 294.  Attendances in 1863 had grown to 104 students. 

The Board of Education was replaced in 1872 by the Education Department (VA 714) under a Minister responsible to Parliament, and so once more the Heidelberg school changed its name – this time to the Heidelberg State School, retaining the school number 294. Education became free, secular, and compulsory.

During 1877-78 the school building and residence were demolished and a new school and five-roomed teachers’ residence was erected on its site. The new building could accommodate over 150 students and with girls and boys now taught together, the school became co-educational.

By 1921 enrolment had grown to more than 270 and some classes were being held in the Methodist Church.  Lobbying by the school community resulted in the construction of seven new classrooms and the complete refurbishment of the existing buildings. The construction was completed in 1923.  A Mother’s Club was formed in 1927, and they raised funds for a swimming pool and other school facilities. 

During the 1950s, student numbers began to rise again, and temporary huts were brought in to serve as classrooms. As new schools opened in the area, enrolments declined, and the huts were no longer needed for teaching. They were instead repurposed as a separate infant school, hall, canteen, and art centre.

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Heidelberg Primary School. 

As of 2025, Heidelberg Primary School remains in operation, with an enrolment of 525 students in 2023. Funding for the construction of a new gymnasium and learning centre was allocated in the 2023–24 State Budget, with completion scheduled for late 2026.
title: Heidelberg Primary School (School No. 294; previously known as Heidelberg National School 1854 – 1862; Heidelberg Common School 1862 – 1872; Heidelberg State School 1872 – 1970)

description:
Fish Creek and District Primary School (School No. 3028) (VA 5480) is a co-educational school located in the West Gippsland region of Victoria.  

The origins of the school date back to the late 19th century. Clearing and settlement of the area by European settlers began in the mid-1880s, and by the end of the decade the population had increased, in large part due to the construction of the Great Southern Railway, such that the need for a school was apparent.

Locals first petitioned the Minister of Education for the establishment of a school in May 1889, and per recommendation of the District Inspector, a building owned by James O’Leary on Fall’s Road was rented to the Education Department (VA 714) for £9 per annum. Fish Creek State School (School No. 3028) first opened here in July 1890. 

In January 1892 the Head Teacher and the District Inspector agreed that the school should be relocated, due to it not being a central enough location, and being in close proximity to a dwelling next door; students’ work was disturbed by conversations heard through the dividing partition.
  
W.P. Ryan had agreed to erect a suitable building on his property and accepted a rental amount of £7 per annum for its use. The 24ft x 10ft building was completed 25 April 1892 and was occupied soon after with an attendance of 18 students. 

In October 1894, Ryan served the Education Department with 3 months notice of intention to terminate the lease of the building. In December of the same year, Michael Synan offered to erect a larger building for the school on his property,  and to lease it for £6 per annum. The Department accepted the offer and the school was run in the new 26ft x 14ft wooden building from 21 January 1895. 

In late 1899, the school reached an attendance of 34 and the need for more space was a pressing issue. The Department purchased a 1-acre site along Waratah Road for £25 and had a new school building erected to house up to 50 pupils, the structure to be 30ft x 18ft. The school re-opened on the 8th of August, 1901. The building was closed for renovations between 23 January – 26 March in 1915, during which time the school was held in the local Mechanic’s Institute, rented to the Department for 15 shillings per week.
 
In August 1924, the District Inspector advised that the current school site was too small. The school committee suggested purchasing three acres along the main road, which the Government Valuer described as “probably the best in the township”. The land was purchased on 15 July 1925 for £280. The school building, shelter pavilion and out-houses were removed from the old site and re-erected on the new, then subsequently repaired. New fencing and a new out-house were built. Whilst undergoing these renovations, the school once again operated out of the Mechanics Institute. The new 30ft x 13ft wooden school building was opened some time in November 1925, and the old site was sold for £50.

Enrolments continued to grow. By March 1928, 77 students were in attendance, despite the school only having accommodation for 50. 

In August 1928, it was approved that the former Mirboo West Primary School (School No. 3371) building be removed and re-erected at Fish Creek to ease overcrowding. However, there was a delay of many months and by May 1929, younger students had to be taught in the open shelter pavilion. From June 11th to December 11th 1929, the local hall was rented to teach the overflow students. The Mirboo West building was finally removed and re-erected on the site in January 1930. 

From 1932 – 35 there were repeated calls from the School Committee to have a teacher’s residence built on the school site. This request was approved in June 1936 and the four-room wooden residence was completed the next year, with occupation from the Head Teacher starting June 28th 1937.

By the late 1940s, the number of enrolments at the school were once again outpacing available accommodation. In May 1947 the School Committee wrote to the Education Department requesting another school building be added from a closed school. This request was approved November 1947, and in September the following year the school building and pavilion from Hoddle Range State School (School No. 3220)  were moved to the Fish Creek site. 

Just a few years later, in February 1953, the Inspector of Schools wrote to the Department stating the need for more classrooms at Fish Creek as the area was becoming further developed and school buses brought children from across the district. A visit to the school from the Minister in May of that year saw them comment that the school was “very crowded”. In March 1954, the Education Department was able to provide a pre-fabricated timber building and schooling began in this new unit, including a classroom and office, April 27th of that year.

In 1962 when enrolments reached 200 pupils, a new wing with two additional classrooms and an office was added to the site.  

At some stage, the name changed from State School to Primary School. This likely occurred in 1970, as there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school’s name was changed to Fish Creek Primary School. Whilst there was no formal announcement regarding the name change, Victoria Government Gazette notices from around this time reflect the change.

In 1975, the school received a $3500 grant to establish a Library/Resource Centre.

1977, a shelter shed from the closed Agnes Primary School (School No. 3043) (VA 5378) and the Walkerville Primary School (School No. 4693) shelter shed were erected. The same year, the school also acquired a portable classroom.

Fish Creek Primary School (School No. 3028) and Yanakie Primary School (School No. 4842) (VA 3896) officially merged on 31 December 1993 to form Fish Creek Primary School with a new school number, No. 5391, on the Fish Creek site. Prior to the merge, the School Council wrote to the Department requesting that the school retain its original school number. Thus, the merged school changed its entity number back to School No. 3028 on 1 January 1994. Fish Creek Primary School voted to change their name to Fish Creek and District Primary School in September 1993. However, they did not seek approval from the Department, so the official name change did not occur until the following year. 

In 1994 the teacher’s residence was removed from the site. The school received a heritage overlay from the South Gippsland Shire Council in 2006, a status which was then abandoned in 2008.

In 2019, a new architect-designed modular building was erected on the school site. 

As of 2024, the school is still operational.
title: Fish Creek and District Primary School (School No. 3028; previously known as Fish Creek State School 1890 – c. 1970; Fish Creek Primary School c. 1970 - 1993)

description:
Quambatook Group School was a small rural school located in Quambatook, Northwest Victoria.
The town’s first ‘official’ school, No. 2443 opened as Quambatook State School in 1909 in a small wooden building on River Street. Extensive alterations were made to the school building in 1922, including the addition of a classroom and office.

In 1948 the school became Quambatook Group School; like consolidated schools, Group Schools were formed by several small rural schools combining into one central school, though with a total number of pupils not exceeding 200. The new Group School moved to a 101 acre site on Charlton Road, south of the town. School buildings from Oakvale (School No. 2717), Quambatook East (School No. 3550), Talgitcha (School No. 3347), Dumosa (School No. 2220), and Ultima East (School No. 4411) were moved to the new site to accommodate the Group School. The school building from Gredgwin (School No. 2290) was also moved to Quambatook to be used as a woodwork room, but was demolished in 1968.

A cricket pitch and tennis courts were added to the school in 1952 and 1954. In 1952 an assistant’s residence was provided, and in 1960 the Quambatook RSL built a memorial at the school consisting of brick-edged flower beds and a flagpole.

In 1995, enrolment was 52. The school received a $20,000 Rural Redevelopment Grant to upgrade facilities, and repainted, refloored and extended the main building.

By 2017, enrolment had fallen to only 6, and the school was de-staffed. Regional staff were appointed temporarily; however, the school was officially closed in 2019.
title: Quambatook Group School (School No. 2443; previously known as Quambatook State School 1909 - 1948)

description:
Casterton Primary School (School No. 2058) (VA 5482) is a single campus co-educational primary school located in the township of Casterton, on the western district Victoria. It serves a historical rural community. 

The school has its origins in 1857, when a non-vested Church of England school was opened in Casterton, on a 1.5-acre site. This school was managed by the Denominational School Board (VA 703) until 1862, when, through the Common Schools Act, the Victorian Parliament abolished the two existing centralised boards and created a single Board of Education (VA 713).  With the passing of this act, the school was re-named Casterton Common School and was given the number 134.

The Education Act 1872 established the Victorian Education Department (VA 714) and introduced free, compulsory and secular schooling for Victorian children. Common School No. 134 was accordingly officially struck off the role on 30 April 1878 and was immediately succeeded by Casterton State School, School No. 2058, which continued to operate on the same site and under the same Head Teacher. A new brick building had been provided in 1877 to accommodate increased student numbers, which was extended in the following years. 

In 1915, a Higher Elementary School was opened in a wooden building on the same site as Casterton State School. In 1953, the Higher Elementary School officially became Casterton High School (School No. 7695; subsequently known as Casterton Secondary College). After the High School moved to a new building on Mount Gambier Rd in 1956, the former Higher Elementary School site became an Infant Department for the State School. 

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Casterton Primary School. 

At the end of 1996, due to declining enrolments, the nearby Strathdownie Primary School (School No. 2883) (VA 5643) was closed and merged with Casterton Primary School on the Casterton site.

As of 2025, Casterton Primary School continues to operate, with approximately 110 enrolled students.
title: Casterton Primary School (School No. 2058; previously known as Casterton Church of England School 1857 – 1862; Casterton Common School No. 134 1862 – 1878; Casterton State School 1878 – c.1970)

description:
Killara Primary School (School No. 5352) (VA 5483) opened in 1993 in a rapidly expanding area of housing estates on the northwest fringe of Sunbury, within the City of Hume. The school is situated on extensive grounds and comprises two core buildings, which include an administration area, 16 classrooms, a library/resource centre, performing and visual arts spaces, a gymnasium, a theatre space, and 10 relocatable classrooms.

Between 1993 and 2000, Killara Primary School experienced rapid growth, with enrolments rising from 103 students to a peak of 641.

By 2024 the school’s enrolment stood at 269 students, and it remains in operation in 2025.
title: Killara Primary School (School No. 5352)

description:
Dandenong South Primary School (School No. 4810) (VA 5484) is a co-educational primary school located in the south-eastern suburbs of Melbourne.   

Requests for a school in the region were made as early as 1954, and in 1956 the Education Department (VA 714) purchased a site for that purpose. By 1959 it was reported that there could be 500 children of school age and under that would attend a new school if provided, and in 1960 work finally commenced on the erection of an eight-classroom school building. The school officially opened in April 1961, as Dandenong South State School. 

In 1970, there was a statewide decision to change the use of the term ‘State School’ to refer to all primary, secondary and technical schools instead of just primary schools, and for all primary schools to use ‘Primary School’ in the name. Accordingly, the school name was changed to Dandenong South Primary School. 

As of 2025, Dandenong South Primary School continues to operate. There is a kindergarten onsite, coordinated in partnership with the City of Greater Dandenong (VA 3690) and Best Chance Family Care.
title: Dandenong South Primary School (School No. 4810; previously known as Dandenong South State School 1961 – c.1970)

description:
Keysborough Secondary College (School No. 8867) (VA 5485) is a co-educational secondary school in Melbourne’s southeast.

The school was established in 2009, through the merger of four schools in the area: Chandler Secondary College (School No. 7712), Heatherhill Secondary College (School No. 7903), Coomoora Secondary College (School No. 8326), and Springvale Secondary College (School No. 8325). Before it officially opened, the school’s interim name was Keysborough Springvale Secondary College.

Each of the former school sites became a campus of the new Keysborough Secondary College, named after the former schools. In 2010 the Heatherhill Campus was renamed Banksia and the Chandler Campus was renamed Acacia, and over the course of 2011 both the Springvale and Coomoora campuses were closed. 

From 2017 to 2019, works were completed at the Acacia campus to construct new hospitality, arts and technology areas, and at the Banksia Campus to update the performing arts and physical education facilities.

As of 2025, Keysborough Secondary College continues to operate, with approximately 2000 students across its two campuses. 

This school should not be confused with Keysborough Secondary College (School No. 7213) (VA 3778), the former Keysborough Technical School which was closed in 1992.
title: Keysborough Secondary College (School No. 8867)

description:
